topicName: Virtual Texture Streaming and GPU Memory Management
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Virtual Texture Streaming and GPU Memory Management in Unreal Engine"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As open-world environments and asset fidelities scale to unprecedented levels, traditional texture memory management falls short. Unreal Engine addresses this challenge through Virtual Texture Streaming (VTS), a powerful rendering technique that allows projects to utilize massive textures with minimal memory footprints by loading only the visible mip levels into VRAM."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Virtual Texture Streaming"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Virtual Texturing breaks down high-resolution textures into smaller, uniformly sized tiles (typically 128x128 pixels). Unlike standard mipmapping which loads complete lower-resolution textures, VTS evaluates what is currently visible on screen and streams only the required tiles from disk into a physical texture cache residing on the GPU."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tile-based caching significantly reduces the VRAM footprint for massive landscapes and complex materials."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Eliminates traditional texture streaming bottlenecks by decoupling surface resolution from physical memory limits."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports Runtime Virtual Textures (RVT) for blending complex material layers dynamically across meshes and landscapes."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Virtual Texture Memory Pools"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"GPU memory management for virtual textures relies heavily on defined memory pools. You can configure and monitor these pools using the Unreal Engine console. To optimize your VRAM budget, adjust the virtual texture pools in your project settings or via the console."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"r.VT.MaxUploadsPerFrame 16
r.VT.Pool.MegaPoolSizeInMB 2048
r.VT.Pool.Aniso 4"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Profiling and Debugging VTS"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When optimizing GPU memory, visual feedback is crucial. Unreal Engine provides built-in visualization tools to inspect how virtual texture tiles are being streamed and rendered in real-time."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"stat VirtualTextureMemory
r.DebugNameplate 0
showflag.VirtualTexturing 1"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the console command "stat VirtualTextureMemory" to open the dedicated memory tracking window. Look out for tile thrashing, which occurs when the physical cache size is too small for the camera velocity and FOV, causing continuous streaming disk reads."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always enable VT support selectively on massive assets like 8K or 16K landscape detail maps rather than small prop textures."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Balance the MegaPoolSizeInMB against your target hardware platform VRAM limits (e.g., lower pools for consoles or mid-range GPUs)."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Combine Runtime Virtual Texturing with World Partition to ensure optimal streaming performance in large-scale open worlds."}]
